messages:
Maya: Quick sync — we need to lock the QoS contracting approach for Hosted vs Dedicated before the PRD goes final. Customers are pushing for per-route SLOs + explicit graceful-degrade behavior. I sketched a lightweight proposal below, trying to balance dev complexity with predictable economics. Can folks sign off or call out blockers by EOD? :eyes:

Sam: skimmed. high-level looks reasonable but we need measurable baselines. our p95s vary a lot by seq len and model. we should define the seq-length-buckets that SLOs apply to, otherwise it's a deployment nightmare. also autoscaler cooldowns will mask short bursts.

Maya: good point. proposal assumes 0-512, 512-1024, 1024+ buckets. if that's too granular we can compress into 2 buckets. thoughts?

Li: SRE: +1 on buckets. also request: tie error-budget burn to alerting and to automatic degrade path. i.e. when 7d error budget burn rate > 2x, trigger canary rollback + route shedding. we should specify windows (5m, 1h, 7d) for different actions.

Ana: from quality side: graceful degrade must include a validation step so we don't return hallucinated short responses when swapping to smaller models. please add a quick eval hook that samples 1% of responses during degrade and compares key NLU metrics; if quality drop > X, revert.

Jordan: enterprise note — customers on Dedicated will expect contractual SLOs per-tenant, and we will need to link this to billing/credits. Also some customers insist on no model-fallback without explicit consent for regulated workloads. we need a per-customer opt-out flag.

Maya: incorporating all that. here's the proposal snippet i mentioned for the PRD (quick YAML) — please call out missing pieces:

```
qos:
  buckets:
    - name: short
      token_range: 0-512
    - name: medium
      token_range: 513-1024
    - name: long
      token_range: 1025-99999
  tiers:
    - name: P0
      p50: 80ms
      p95: 200ms
      error_budget: 0.1%
    - name: P1
      p50: 120ms
      p95: 350ms
      error_budget: 0.5%
    - name: P2
      p50: 250ms
      p95: 800ms
      error_budget: 1.5%
degrade:
  fallback_model: smaller-1
  validation_hook: perf_and_quality_check
  validation_sample_rate: 0.01 # 1%
  rollback_on_quality_drop_pct: 8
  shed_routes: ["non-critical-embeddings", "low-priority-batch"]
autoscale:
  cooldowns:
    scale_up: 30s
    scale_down: 4m
alerts:
  windows:
    - name: immediate
      window: 5m
      action: page
    - name: medium
      window: 1h
      action: reduce_traffic_route
    - name: sustained
      window: 7d
      action: contract_review
```

Sam: need to know what 'smaller-1' maps to (quantized variant? fewer layers?). also the validation hook needs to be light-weight — 1% sampling might still add tail latency. maybe do async verification for quality and only hold degrade for the first N requests (N=50) synchronously.

Li: agree with async. operational triggers we propose:
- 5m p50/p95 breach: soft-alert (tickets, no page)
- 1h sustained breach or 5m error spike: page oncall + start route-shedding policy
- 7d burn > threshold: escalate to exec + open capacity contract review

Ana: for quality evaluation, i'll add a tiny eval harness that computes BLEU/ROUGE or a small fingerprint similarity metric depending on task. we should store sampled responses for audits. add data-retention note in PRD.

Jordan: for Dedicated customers: add a per-tenant "no-fallback" flag and a contract field listing allowed fallback models. default: allow fallback for hosted, deny for regulated dedicated unless approved.

deploy-bot: deploy: qos-contracting/proposal v0.3 pushed to /infra/rfc — CI passed :white_check_mark:

Maya: next steps I propose:
- Sam: map fallback_model names to actual binary/quantization variants and add perf matrix (owner)
- Li: add precise alert windows + playbook snippets (owner)
- Ana: implement lightweight eval harness + retention policy (owner)
- Jordan: draft contract wording for per-tenant SLOs and fallback opt-out (owner)
- Maya: fold into PRD + open RFC for final review by end of week

Please confirm ownership here or call out if timelines are unrealistic. :thumbsup:
